newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's president Lee meets Tibet's Dalai Lama.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's president Lee meets Tibet's Dalai Lama.

text.p: Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, met Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui on Thursday, capping a six-day religious tour on a political note certain to anger communist China.

Government sources said the men greeted each other warmly at the Foreign Ministry's walled Taipei Guest House, a downtown venue chosen to avoid the political sensitivities of a more formal meeting at the presidential office.
"President Lee greeted the Dalai Lama at the door with a warm handshake," said an official photographer who witnessed the meeting. "They entered the room and posed for some pictures."
While the two exchanged greetings in English, Lee presented the Tibetan Buddhist god-king a crystal statue bearing the likeness of the Dalai Lama, the witness said.
Substantive discussions had not yet begun when the photographer was asked to leave the room.

Even before Lee's aides confirmed on Wednesday that the Dalai Lama and Lee would meet, the long-rumoured encounter already had angered Beijing, which assailed it as the collusion of two "splittists" bent on independence from China for both Tibet and Nationalist-ruled Taiwan.

The Dalai Lama arrived on Saturday for an unprecedented visit billed as a religious tour. It was his first return to Chinese soil since he fled his Himalayan homeland in 1959 after the failure of an uprising against Chinese rule of Tibet.

The Dalai Lama and Lee deny seeking independence from China. The Tibetan leader has said he wants only self-rule for Tibet. Lee espouses Taiwan's reunification with the mainland but not before Beijing embraces democracy.
